title.narrative: Economic Management Improvement Program, Phase 2 (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The proposed Economic Management Improvement Program, Phase 2 (EMIP II) supports transformation of Uzbekistan's state-dominated economy by strengthening fiscal management,improving governance and operations of state-owned enterprises (SOEs), and enhancing public sector accountability. The program is aligned with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) countrypartnership strategy for Uzbekistan, 2019-2023 and operational priorities of ADB's Strategy 2030 that are (i) strengthening governance, quality, and capacity of public institutions to undertakepolicy reforms and promote private sector development; (ii) accelerating progress in gender equality; (iii) addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities; and (iv) tackling climatechange, building climate and disaster resilience, and enhancing environmental sustainability.The program is designed under a policy-based lending modality with two subprograms. While subprogram 1 focuses on improving the legal, regulatory, and institutional framework, subprogram 2 supports measures for effective and transparent fiscal management; SOE transformation, including strengthening of the competitive environment; and improving anticorruption and audit systems. The programmatic approach allows for comprehensive policy dialogue and flexibility in implementing logically sequenced structural reforms in a multiyear framework. The attached technical assistance (TA) of $250,000 supports the implementation.

Reports and Recommendations of the President
09 Feb 2023 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-approves-150-million-loan-improve-economic-management-uzbekistan

ACA implemented an electronic grievance redressal mechanism, which allows filing of grievances on corruption by citizens and established a public council, comprising at least 10% female membership, to strengthen public sector accountability. (Document required: ACA report, confirming implementation of the grievance redressal mechanism and activities of the public council)

COA implemented an IT platform for integrating activities of all financial audit bodies and internal audit services to (i) reduce human factor in control processes, (ii) streamline inspections of budgetary organizations by monitoring repeated inspections and interference, and (iii) improve the efficiency, transparency, and objectivity of control measures. (Document required: COA report, confirming implementation of IT platform)

Cabinet of Ministers submitted (i) the State Property Management Law and (ii) the Privatization Law to the Parliament to establish criteria for public sector assets that will remain under state ownership and streamline the privatization process. (Document required: Copies of the State Property Management Law and the Privatization Law with the letters from the Cabinet of Ministers on submission to the Parliament)

Effective in 2022, at least 12 SOEsc transitioned from national financial reporting standards and prepared and publicly disclosed IFRS-based financial reports with appropriate notes to improve transparency on financial performance. (Document required: MOF and SAMA reports on implementation of IFRS in selected SOEs)
Loan 4292: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 15 May 2025

MOF and SAMA (i) approved a corporate governance assessment tool (score card) based on OECD guidelines to be used on an annual basis and (ii) implemented the score card effective from 2022 in at least 20 SOEs. (Document required: MOF and SAMA reports on the implementation of the score card)
TA 10092: 15% disbursed as of 15 May 2025
Tenders and Contracts Awarded: https://www.adb.org/projects/51350-004/main#project-tenders

The MOF operationalized a methodology for assessment of risks related to liabilities of SOEs to improve transparency of SOE financing. (Document required: Cabinet of Ministers Resolution and MOF internal order on the operationalization of the methodology)

The State Tax Committee established and operationalized (i) a mandatory system for registration of electronic invoices for all business entities, (ii) an electronic VAT taxpayer registration system, (iii) a cashback system by registering cash receipts for purchases made by individuals in retail, catering, and personal services in a mobile application to increase tax collection and voluntary tax compliance, and (iv) the E-IMTIYOZ system to monitor the recipients of tax incentives and benefits. (Document required: State Tax Committee report on the implementation of i-iv, including government resolutions)

The government (i) approved the Strategic Framework on Green Economy, 2022-2030 and the long-term action plan for improving energy efficiency, conservation of natural resources, reduction in greenhouse gas emissions, access to green energy, and gender responsive green jobs generation and training of the labor force in line with green economy, and (ii) established a functioning inter-ministerial council and technical secretariat, operative since 2022 to coordinate across responsible ministries and oversee the implementation of the strategy. (Document required: Government Resolution on Strategic Framework on Green Economy, 2022-2030, including establishment of the inter-ministerial council, and government order on the establishment of the technical secretariat)

The government adopted criteria based on (i) competitive, (ii) transparent, and (iii) merit-based selection of independent supervisory board members at SOEs, including female board representation and commenced its implementation effective in 2022 to strengthen professional management of SOEs. (Document required: Government resolution, which includes the selection criteria and the SAMA report on female representation at SOE supervisory boards)

The government adopted the minimum consumer spending as a uniform criterion, effective since 2022, to determine the level of need for assignment of benefits for low-income families and operationalized an automated and sex-disaggregated Social Protection Single Registry for identifying the beneficiaries and distributing the benefits. (Document required: Resolution of the government on the criterion adopted and sex-disaggregated report on beneficiaries under the Social Protection Single Registry)

The government strengthened the AMC’s regulatory and enforcement powers through implementation of a government resolution to prevent unreasonable and artificial price increases for socially significant monopoly goods, including those sold on commodity exchanges in conditions of sharp price fluctuations, and (ii) AMC implemented anti-monopoly compliance mechanism in at least 20 SOEs with a dominant position in their relevant markets to promote competition.b (Document required: (i) Government resolution on preventing artificial price increases, and (ii) government resolution on the anti-monopoly compliance mechanism, internal rules of SOEs on the antimonopoly compliance mechanism, and the AMC report on implementation of the anti-monopoly compliance mechanism)

The supervisory boards of JSC Agrobank, JSC Qishloq Qurilish Bank and JSC Xalq Bank established KPIs with continuing effective implementation in 2022 and appointed at least one independent supervisory board member to improve operational and financial performance in line with their approved transformation strategies and roadmaps. (Document required: List of KPIs and a report on the implementation of KPIs, list of independent supervisory board members and approved transformation strategies)
